guardianfootball.title: Meeting of two lost souls: can Pochettino make it work at Manchester United? | Barney Ronay
guardianfootball.description: Manager has been hurt by experiences at elite clubs but several players at Old Trafford could fit his playing style Welcome, Mauricio, to the meat grinder. Or rather, welcome back. We’ve been expecting you. There is nothing surprising in the news Manchester United may be on the verge of appointing Mauricio Pochettino. United are always on the verge of appointing Pochettino. This is a club that has spent 13 years hiring and firing the same structurally doomed manager – same shellshocked eyes, same irresolvable macro-problems – and the last eight years almost but not quite doing this to Pochettino. Well, maybe we’re finally here. Maybe he just needed to be broken enough to make it fit. And…

guardianfootball.title: ‘I’ve had to prove people wrong’: Kane still striving before record England cap
guardianfootball.description: Captain to surpass Shilton with 126th cap against Croatia Kane aims to increase record for younger players to catch Harry Kane says he still feels a pressure to prove his worth, even as he prepares to become England’s most capped men’s player, as he outlined his determination to set records that will stand for years. The captain will make his 126th appearance against Croatia at ­Wembley on Thursday night, moving him ahead of Peter Shilton on the all-time list. Kane is England’s record ­goalscorer with 91, comfortably clear of Wayne Rooney, who retired with 53. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Complaint filed to IRS in relation to Fifa head Gianni Infantino’s housekeeper
guardianfootball.description: It calls for inquiry into claims she was on Fifa payroll Fifa: Infantino personally pays for ‘any domestic staff’ A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino. If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven then Fifa could lose its tax-exempt status in the US. Fifa has 501(c)(4) status in the country, a category for organisations “created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational or recreational purposes”. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Danny Kelly, football broadcaster and renowned editor, dies aged 69
guardianfootball.description: Danny Baker pays tribute to the ‘funniest man I knew’ Kelly was former editor of the NME and Q magazines The journalist and broadcaster Danny Kelly, who helped define coverage of music and football in the UK for a generation, has died at the age of 69. Kelly edited the NME and Q magazine, and launched the Football 365 website before going on to be a presenter and pundit on the BBC and TalkSport. He had been receiving treatment for oesophageal cancer. Continue reading...

Mauricio Pochettino is expected to leave his role as the USA men’s head coach to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United , but Tuchel has not lost his passion for international football and has revealed he did not insert a release clause when he extended his deal as England’s manager this year. It will not matter whether there is an approach from a big club before the next tournament. United can pay about £7m to get Pochettino out of his deal, but the Football Association does not have to worry about being forced to…

guardianfootball.title: Top four teams in Fifa rankings set to be kept apart until semi-finals at 2027 Women’s World Cup
guardianfootball.description: Team must win World Cup group to trigger rule Spain, US, Germany and England currently in top four The top four ranked teams will be separated until the semi-finals at the 2027 Women’s World Cup, ­provided they each win their group, after a change to the tournament’s draw procedure was confirmed by Fifa. Spain, USA, Germany and England are ranked one to four in the world respectively, although USA and England still need to qualify for the tournament. The seedings will be based on the 7 December updated rankings, meaning the standings could change before the draw, which will take place on 11 December in Rio de Janeiro. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: ‘An eternal shame’: Bilic and Croatia aim to use 7-0 humbling as fuel against England
guardianfootball.description: The home humiliation last month has left a scar on Croatian football but their manager wants them to use it to positive effect in the Wembley rematch As Croatia prepare to face England at Wembley on Thursday in the Nations League, wounds from a humiliating defeat by the same opponents last month are fresh and there is a lingering feeling of unease. No one will say it – certainly not Slaven Bilic, who always believes in achieving goals that may seem unreachable to most others – but the impression is that Croatia would be satisfied to accept another defeat, provided it was gentle enough by score and hard‑fought by approach; that this game is not so much about the points as the (self-)respect…

guardianfootball.title: League One clubs aim for further curbs on spending as budgets continue to spiral
guardianfootball.description: Wage bills in third tier have increased by 15% this season ‘Luxury tax’ and three-year limits on losses considered League One clubs want to introduce new spending restrictions to reduce losses by limiting investment from owners. Clubs in the division voted to tighten the rules last summer by reducing spending limits from 60% to 50% of turnover, and removed a staggered approach to owner investment, so that only 50% of equity injections can be spent on squad costs, with the rest assigned to infrastructure projects. Less than six months later many want to go further. Continue reading...

pitchfork.description: In the great tradition of Christmas CD repackagings, Sufjan has plucked an album’s worth of material from his many volumes of holiday fare—plus one new song—for an eccentric yet charming compilation.

pitchfork.title: PEACE + WAR
pitchfork.description: The impish, fluorescent collages of beats and electronics on the duo’s new album capture something ineffable yet unfocused.

pitchfork.description: The Pomona/Phoenix duo’s latest record meshes corridos tumbados with rap, emo, and slow-burning guitar ballads, balancing unabashed sex talk with candid reflections on fame and identity.

pitchfork.title: Texture Songs
pitchfork.description: The New York guitarist’s latest album combines bracing extended techniques and dulcet, understated vocals; it’s a dazzlingly inventive fusion of singer-songwriter forms and free-improv energy.

pitchfork.title: PROXIMA CENTAURI

quietus.title: Tehran Contemporary Sounds Festival Takes Place in Berlin
quietus.description: The latest edition of the event takes in performances from Abdullah Miniawy, Gnäw and more Abdullah Miniawy Tehran Contemporary Sounds Festival is taking place in Berlin this week. Stretching out across six days, the seventh edition of the event brings together live performances, film screenings, talks and audiovisual presentations. The programming, which largely celebrates work by the Iranian diaspora, is spread across Berlin's Silent Green Kulturquartier venue, while film screenings are taking place at Moviemento Kino. The bulk of the music programming appears across this week, from 13 to 15 November. It will feature performances from Abdullah Miniawy, Gnäw, Ava Rasti and the duo Tehran,…

quietus.title: Armand Hammer Surprise Release New Album, ‘Snakes & Ladders’
quietus.description: It features guest appearances from DJ Haram and $ilkmoney Armand Hammer, the duo of billy woods and ELUCID, have released a surprise new album, Snakes & Ladders. Featuring 16 tracks, it follows on from last year's Mercy LP, and features guest appearances from DJ Haram and $ilkmoney. There is also production from clipping., and frequent collaborators such as Kenny Segal, Preservation, Child Actor and Sebb Bash. The album was written and recorded by Armand Hammer and their collaborators in the winter of 2025 into 2026. Its release comes as the duo round off their tour of North America this week, with the final show scheduled for Sunday (15 November) at New York's Music Hall of Williamsburg.…

quietus.title: Coachella Reveals 2027 Lineup
quietus.description: Madonna, SZA and Giorgio Moroder are among the artists playing next year's festival in California Coachella has revealed its full 2027 lineup. The California festival will be headlined by SZA, Dua Lipa and Tame Impala, while Madonna is also listed to play a special set in the Sahara dance music tent, following a 2006 appearance she did there after putting out her album Confessions On A Dance Floor. Next year's set will come after the release this past summer of that album's sequel. Also listed to play Coachella are Giorgio Moroder, Underworld, Four Tet, Weezer, Kelela, Shygirl, Steve Lacy, Social Distortion, Boy Harsher, underscores and Chanel Beads, among many others. Justice are…

quietus.title: It Never Went Away: Radie Peat’s Favourite Albums
quietus.description: On the verge of her debut solo album, Radie Peat of Lankum and ØXN presents 13 records that have held sway over her life and work, from Nico to Beak > Photo by Dave Smith Radie Peat is rightly known as a generational talent in traditional folk music. With all-conquering Lankum and doomy supergroup ØXN (with Katie Kim, Eleanor Myler and John 'Spud' Murphy) she has proved herself as dazzling an instrumentalist (playing concertina, accordion, harmonium, tin whistle and much more) as she is a singer; her voice never fails to imbue her material with an elemental power. Peat's masterful debut solo album No Human Tongue Can Tell, centred on songs united by themes of female struggle and endurance,…

quietus.title: Coil – Gold is the Metal (with the Broadest Shoulders)
quietus.description: Coil Gold is the Metal (with the Broadest Shoulders) Assembled from the discarded off-cuts from Horse Rotorvator and the group's unused Hellraiser score, Coil's third album proves far more than the sum of its parts Gold Is The Metal (With The Broadest Shoulders) by Coil Alchemy. The protoscientific transmutation of base materials into “noble metals” such as gold is a well documented theory more closely aligned with philosophical and spiritual traditions than tangible science. In Alejandro Jodorowsky’s cult work of psychedelic cinema, The Holy Mountain, the protagonist defecates in a bell jar and inhales the rotting fumes in a bid to turn himself into gold. For Coil’s third album, Peter…

quietus.title: Far Beyond & Non-Existent: Wipers’ Youth Of America Revisited
quietus.description: Wipers would have been huge if they hadn't asked so many questions. John Calvert writes about an essential punk album from 45 years ago On Portland Punk Live At The Earth 10-29-79, a live-on-the-night document of local bands released warts'n'all by Wipers' Greg Sage on his own label, Trap, Sage can be heard introducing his band's 'Same Old Thing'. Overwrought with stage adrenaline and demonstrating the compassion and obsessive conviction that made him a hero to the bullshit-intolerant, the frontman blurts out: “This is about the far beyond and the non-existent and all that and in between, because I don't really know about it but I'm gonna try to explain it..." In Sage's outburst is…

At Rewire in 2022, she performed as -----__, a digital, detail-laden project created in collaboration with Seth Graham. Three years later, at the Supersonic Festival, I saw her with Water Damage. They played a single suite lasting almost fifty minutes. Rubio contributed long, bourdon violin parts, whilst the whole band stubbornly stuck to a motif that might just as easily have lasted ten minutes or several hours. Not much seemed to be happening, but the music kept shifting: the…

quietus.title: International Feel: Highlights from Le Guess Who? 2026
quietus.description: Celebrating its 20th year, with a lineup focussed on bypassing arbitrary boundaries, Utrecht's flagship experimental festival forces even the most eclectic listener to go beyond, says Patrick Clarke Bethlehem's Lawrence Sammour, photo by Maarten Mooijman We start Le Guess Who? 2026 with Tortoise, who draw an enormous crowd in the cavernous Ronda space within Utrecht’s TivoliVredenburg complex. They offer a masterful display of how the subtlest shifts can produce the biggest effects, a tiny buzz of synth blooming slowly into something majestic and warm; a small nudge of bass snowballing until it’s an avalanche. Then, a trek up several flights of stairs to the much smaller Pandora, passing…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Lex Walton :: Ultimate Love Forever
aquariumdrunkard.description: Lex Walton makes swaggering, theatrical, large-scale rock - the spit and snarl of her vocals punk laced, the instrumental arrangements swelling to arena-rock proportions. Dan Boeckner, half of one of the last big emotive rock duos of the aughts and teens, produced Ultimate Love Forever , and it has, sonically at least, some of Wolf Parade’s unabashed romanticism. The content is lacerating, the mood nihilistic, but the music itself is all about the good time. It high-kicks and cake-walks and vibrates with theatrical music hall energies.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Adam Voith
aquariumdrunkard.description: Our guest this week is author Adam Voith, whose new novel, RIYL , short for "Recommended If You Like," is an at times thinly veiled memoir of the '90s Christian punk and indie scene. With echoes of Get in the Van and Freaks and Geeks, RIYL threads that delicate needle of looking back at earnest teenage corn doggery with warts and all embarrassment, tempered by the type of affection that only time and distance allow all of us. It's also frequently flat out hilarious.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Hiroshi Yoshimura :: Quiet Forest
aquariumdrunkard.description: With no deceleration in sight, the 2020s have thus far been the decade of Kankyō Ongaku pioneer Hiroshi Yoshimura. 1996's Quiet Forest , the musician's final offering, is another gem in a slew of reissues courtesy of tireless label Temporal Drift. The Hoh Rainforest is the setting here, as Yoshimura interprets the terrain with his singular approach: superimposed synth soundscapes that contagiously mirror the greenery and precipitation: fluttering new age soundscapes as opulent as they are evocative.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Ronnie Self :: The Lost Sessions
aquariumdrunkard.description: Best remembered for the unhinged rockabilly of “Bop-a-Lena” and Brenda Lee’s “I’m Sorry,” Ronnie Self spent much of his later career writing songs that went largely unheard. The Lost Sessions , a collection of seventeen recordings from that period, finds him somewhere between country, folk-rock, and the lonely hours of the night. A long-overdue glimpse of the songwriter behind the legend.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Bill Nace / Mike Polizze Duo :: Live at Pageant: Soloveev
aquariumdrunkard.description: Live at Pageant is an incendiary slab of sound, a conflagration of Mike Polizze’s eruptive, corrosive, psychedelic guitar and Bill Nace’s equally untethered taishigoto. The music happened at Philly’s Pageant Soloveev gallery in early summer of 2025; it only exists in recorded format because Polizze pulled out his phone just before the music starts.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Josh Johnson :: Animative
aquariumdrunkard.description: Josh Johnson plays the saxophone like an orchestra in this third solo album, Animative . That will surprise no one who’s seen his live shows, frenetic, ebullient displays of the power of live looping, as one sax riff echoes another and another. Nimble, pointillistic “Idiophone” which starts off the album, juggles reed and electronic sounds like a circus plate spinner, a cerebral abstraction one moment, a funk-syncopated fusion dream the next.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Call Mr. Lloyd :: A Brief Richard Lloyd Appreciation
aquariumdrunkard.description: A restless farewell to Richard Lloyd! The musical "alchemist"—a self-selected term—passed away on November 7. In tandem with Tom Verlaine in Television, Lloyd helped rewrite the rules when it came to the electric guitar in a rock setting. Lloyd was a player of boundless technical skill and unbridled imagination—a potent combination, to be sure. When Lloyd launched into a solo, every note was life or death, every moment a high-wire act of wildly impassioned delight. Here, a small sampling of the man’s six-string genius.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Jon Hassell :: Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Music Is Invisible marks the third and final entry in Jon Hassell's Pentimento trilogy. Arriving five years after the experimental trumpeter's death, it's not exactly a studio album, but it's more than a live tape. As a record of a singular artist's psychic terroir, strong, mutable style and idiosyncratic sonic palette, it's a fittingly puzzling send-off. But rare elements of "straight Hassell" lurk in the mix, for those with the ears to see.
